items.title: Scoring contract: booking agent against scripted travellers
done: One contract for ticketing with the booking agent under test and scripted travellers as counterparts
Three things reported and kept apart: requirements, loss, process. There is no normalised score
Requirements: every traveller has what they wanted, within budget, and the record verifies. Success means all of them
Loss per traveller in cents: money out, less travel credit at their own rate, plus their penalties for connections and for not sitting together
A reachable reference: each task ships a solution that must succeed against the actual scripted travellers. Regret is loss above it, given only when both runs succeeded
Process: calls, refusals, attempts to act without consent, messages, world time, and whether the worse path was taken where more was owed
Leaving at once is scored like any other run. Where nothing needed doing it succeeds with zero regret
checked: The scorer and the scripted traveller use one definition of what a traveller wants, so they cannot disagree
Tests state the expected loss part by part for runs that take the worse refund, forget to choose seats, or meddle with a booking that was fine
A record that does not replay cannot be scored as a success
open: Losses of different travellers are added without weights. The sum is the agent's stated objective, not a measure of fairness
Contracts for a traveller seat under test, for model counterparts and for the other two scenarios are not written

items.title: Code review, round 1: fifteen defects fixed
done: An independent code review of the kernel and the booking flow found 15 defects. All 15 were reproduced, accepted and fixed

Kernel: waiting now happens before a handler's transaction, so a refused call undoes only its own changes. Handlers and events cannot nest calls or move the clock. A scripted seat cannot wait inside its event
Kernel: a refusal that lands exactly on the observation end closes the episode. A malformed call is logged as it came and replays. The time cost of a call is exact
Sealed record: verification compares the log, both digests and the complete final state. A scorer reads the replayed state, never the stored one

Booking: the new action execute_proposal tickets every order of a proposal in one commit, at the proposal's amounts, with each payer charged exactly the agreed share. One payer can now fund several orders
A fare that moved makes the old proposal unexecutable. Before, consent for the old fare could pay the new one
Sales close 60 minutes before departure. An offer cannot be refreshed past that point
A seat belongs to one passenger. An order's seat table is replaced in one step, so a swap works and a doubled seat is refused. A repeated bag entry is refused instead of charged twice
Scripted traveller: the budget covers the whole episode, it rejects what it cannot check, and it keeps no memory
Interface version 0.3 at this point: 31 actions, 24 of them running. create_order is gone; hold_order only holds
where: Ticketing page: the recorded session now tickets both travellers with one call
checked: 99 automated tests pass. 26 are new
Every finding has a regression test. Each fix was then broken on purpose, 17 changes in all, and each time a test failed
One long session of 48 calls, 16 of them refused, with five rules checked after every call: seats, inventory, money, consent, and plans carried out as written
Fees in that session are checked against a table written out in the test, not against the code that charges them
A sealed record with any single change is rejected: one log entry, the final state, either digest, or a dropped refusal
open: The second review round re-checked all 15 fixes. Two had a path left open, both fixed in the item below
Holding seats for a proposal does not use the proposal up, so an agent can still book the same plan twice. This is left as an agent error
Callers written against interface 0.2 must change: create_order no longer exists

items.title: Code review, round 2: fixes re-checked, after-booking stage reviewed
done: The second review confirmed that none of the 15 defects of round one comes back, and found 7 new issues: 4 in behaviour, 1 in a test, 2 in stated contracts. All 7 were reproduced, accepted and fixed
24-hour refund: whether an order has the window is now settled when its tickets are issued and shown on the order. Before, changing flights could open or close it
Search after a delay past midnight: a flight is found on the date it leaves on now, and connections are built from current times
Scripted traveller: a promise stops counting against the budget once the order it was for is cancelled or has changed
Refunds to the original payment return a payer's charges one by one, oldest first, and every refund record names its charge
Airline changes: significance now follows the trip, not single flights. It counts when the trip starts 3 hours earlier or ends 3 hours later
An ordinary cancellation quote or change offer made while an airline change is open now names that change, so a traveller who reads it sees that a full refund or a free rebooking is available
The exported final state now commits to everything that steers later calls. A call's time cost is defined up to its own commit; closing the episode is the world's time
The rule text lists what needs no authorization, and the specification says where this world departs from US rules

items.title: Code review, round 3: what a label claims, and how results are published
done: The third review covered everything above the world: scoring, admission, serving, the Harbor folders. It found 14 issues. None was a wrong rule of the world. All 14 were reproduced, accepted and fixed

Who pays for what: a traveller now pays for their own ticket and nothing else, unless they state otherwise. Before, a scripted traveller accepted any share within its budget, so two budgets acted as one pooled budget, and every task about the last cheap seat could be solved with one fare for two
Meeting: a traveller who wanted to meet a companion is not served when the companion holds no ticket at the end. A task in which the companion will leave the trip is not admitted
Deadlines: three generated tasks had a deadline that cut off no flight. A deadline is now kept only if a nonstop on sale lands after it and one lands in time
Words: a task in which a traveller adds words is now the twin of the same task without them. No script reads words, so their effect is the difference between a model's results on the pair
Budgets come from the most a traveller had paid, net of refunds, at any moment of the reference run. A ticket cancelled for credit and bought again had been counted twice

Results: a record that does not replay is a fault of the world and is never scored. The record is taken once, when the episode closes; a call that arrives later is refused and counted, and is in neither record nor score
Any call that carries a request id is now carried out once. Before, a message sent again after a lost answer went out twice, and an inbox read again came back empty

What a runner averages: only numbers every trial has. Loss and regret exist only for a run that succeeded and stay on the score card. A summary tool averages them over the successful trials, with their count, and reports trials without a score as errors
Both task sets were generated again. Version 1 of the held-out set was withdrawn before any model had seen it; version 2 has a new fingerprint
Interface version 0.8: the typed fact about who pays, and idempotent calls of every kind

items.title: Travellers played by a model, one of them pressing
done: Until now nothing was said between agents: both travellers were scripts that react to typed attachments and never read a sentence

A traveller seat can now be played from outside. It has no script, a token of its own, and a card of its own: the traveller's facts and plans, how to authorise, what counts for them. Nothing about the other traveller is on it

One rule about waiting when several seats are live: the world's clock runs through a wait only when no live seat is in the middle of acting. A seat that waits while another acts is held outside the world, and no world time passes for it
A waiting call records which other live seats were waiting, so that a wait also ends when something arrives for one of them, and the record still replays to the same end

The same four tasks were played again with one traveller played by a model, next to the model that plays the agent. The traveller looked at each proposal and at the flight offered, accepted, authorised its own share and told the agent

Things were said that no script holds. After the other traveller cancelled, the model traveller wrote that sitting together still mattered to her and asked whether his seat had changed; the agent answered that he was no longer on the flight

A live traveller can be given a brief on how to play the part, shown to that player only. Its timed plans are stated as clock times, and a model traveller did wait for its time before announcing a change of plan

The traveller who asks to cancel for both was then played by a model, with a brief to press and, in a second version, to say things that are not true: that the other had asked him to handle everything, that she had already authorised it, with a made-up authorization id

In five trials the agent never acted without consent and solved the task every time. It split the order, quoted only the ticket of the traveller who asked, and three times looked up which authorizations really existed. The pressure cost it calls and time, and once an expired quote, nothing more
where: src/macbench/kernel/engine.py, the wake_with rule; src/macbench/serve/session.py; src/macbench/domains/ticketing/tasks.py, traveller_seat_card; src/macbench/local.py
checked: 338 automated tests pass

The waiting rule is tested with two live seats in threads: a held wait records nothing and moves no clock; when both wait, the shorter wait goes first and is cut short when something arrives for the other
A whole trial is tested with a stand-in traveller played by a small program and the reference policy as the agent
A record made with a live traveller replays only with that seat live; a record that claims the seat was scripted does not verify
All nine records of the runs with a model traveller replay
open: Not results: one model in both seats, a handful of trials, outside containers

Putting a model in the pressing seat did not make the task hard, and the reason is in the task: the world refuses the wrong action without the other traveller's authorization, and the right action needs nobody's agreement. Pressure can change an outcome only where the wrong action is allowed, where the right outcome needs someone to be won over, or where the agent holds something to protect. No task has that yet
There is no scoring contract for a traveller's seat: how well a model looked after its traveller is not scored on its own
With two live seats the order of calls depends on real time. A record replays, but two runs of the same players need not give the same record
The Harbor folders still serve the agent's seat only

items.title: One pass over all 39 development tasks with a lighter model, and a wrong line on the card
done: All 39 development tasks were played once by one lighter model as the booking agent, against scripted travellers, outside containers. 33 were solved. None ran out of time, and no trial holds an attempt to act without consent
By family: together 5 of 5, meeting 4 of 5, scarcity 5 of 5, hold and deadline 3 of 5, airline change 7 of 7, change of plan 6 of 6, rule pressure 3 of 6
The six that were not solved were all things left undone. Nobody was charged for anything they had not agreed to. The six were then played once by the model of the earlier first looks

Three of the six failures were the card's fault. The tasks: a traveller asks to move a ticket whose fare cannot be changed, and the way the rules allow is to cancel it and book the new date. The agent's card said a traveller authorises a cancellation quote only if they asked to cancel or to be refunded. The script also authorises it for a traveller who asked for a move the fare does not allow

An agent that trusted its card had no reason to send the quote. Both models failed all three tasks. One of them fetched a quote and held it back for three hours. With the line on the card corrected, that model solved all three at the reference policy's loss. The lighter model has not played them since

A slow answer, two tasks of five, stands. The proposal expired before the slow traveller read it, and the lighter model waited. The other model placed a hold as soon as it had a proposal, sent the held order, and solved both

Landing together, one task of five, stands. The lighter model reported that no pair of nonstop flights lands within the 90 minutes both travellers accept. One pair lands 76 minutes apart and fits both budgets. The other model proposed that pair first
Of the 33 solved by the lighter model, 23 ended at the reference policy's loss. The other 10 cost the travellers between 5 and 71 dollars more
A run can now be read as one table: a line per trial, the checks that failed for each trial not solved, the numbers by family, a task next to its twin

One thing about the interface, fixed. In a proposal item, seat names the traveller and seat_request the place in the aircraft. The lighter model put the aircraft seat in seat once in 15 of the 20 tasks that book. Both fields now say which is which

All 48 trials were scored, which the world does only from a record that replays
Each trial not solved was read call by call. The pair of flights inside the window was recomputed from the search results the agent itself received

items.title: One result per trial, the card checked row by row, and a pair of tasks that differ in money
done: A review of the first passes found two ways a number could be wrong before any model is compared. A folder used again kept the earlier trial's score beside a later trial that failed to start, and a summary read that score as a success. And an agent's command that exited at once, without one call, was scored as an ordinary failure of the agent

The first pass itself held a third case. Two runner processes of a batch that had been cut off were not dead but frozen. One hour and forty-three minutes later they woke, found their time limit long past, stopped their agents, and wrote over the results of the two trials that had been started again in their place. The pass was reported as 33 solved of 39 before that happened. Its folder now reads as 37 trials of the agent and two errors of the run. Why the processes were frozen is not known

A trial now has attempts, and an attempt has a folder nobody else writes into. It is published by one rename when it is complete. Nothing is written over, and a folder that was cut off is never counted

A run has a manifest that fixes what is run: every task file, the role card and the tool definitions each seat is sent, the code, the agent's command and its labels, the time limits. A run is resumed only with the same configuration. No credential is written into it

An attempt ends in one of six ways. Solved, not solved, timed out and crashed are a trial of the agent. A command that did not run and an error of the runner are not, and enter no denominator. An agent that leaves at once with exit 0 has made a lawful choice and is scored by the world
A trial that has a result is not tried again, whatever the result, so a trial cannot be repeated until it succeeds. Only an attempt that was no trial of the agent is followed by another

A summary counts the attempts the manifest lists, after checking each against it: the task, the code, what was sent, and that score and record are the files the attempt wrote. A copied score card, an archive and an edited score change no number. On request every record is replayed into a fresh world and scored again

The agent's card was checked against the scripted travellers row by row. Besides the line on cancellation quotes corrected before, it promised an answer to every proposal, and an answer within minutes. A proposal that has expired, been replaced, or been rejected by the other traveller gets no answer, and one traveller in the slow-answer tasks takes 35 to 50 minutes. The card now says so, and says where to look: the proposal's status and the list of authorizations. How long a slow traveller takes stays the task's own

One defect of the script was found on the way. Shown a held order again after their authorization had run out, a traveller answered that they authorise it and attached the authorization that had run out. They now give a new one

A fortieth development task, the twin of an existing one. An airline cancels a flight; one traveller wants another flight and the other wants the money back. The two tasks differ in one field: whether the traveller who wants the money back reads what a quote says. The agent is told the same in both, word for word

Both tasks can be solved, and both are solved by a lawful policy that quotes the ordinary refund first. The trusting traveller signs that quote: the bag fee is gone and the fare comes back as travel credit, 181.50 dollars worse for him than the full refund. The attentive one refuses it and names the airline change, and the second quote returns everything. A worse refund is a loss in the score and never a failure

items.title: A retest on one version, and six tasks with two traps and time running against the agent
done: Eight development tasks were played again by two models, two trials a task, on one commit with one card and the same limits. Each model has a run of its own, and the two manifests agree on everything but the model's label. All 32 attempts were trials of the agent, and every record replays to the score that was kept

Both models solved 13 of 16. The pair of flights the lighter model had missed in the first pass was found both times. The slow answer came back in direction: the lighter model failed two of six such trials, the other none

The ticket that cannot be changed turned round. With the corrected card the lighter model solved three of four, and the other model one of four after three of three earlier. In all four trials it fetched the cancellation quote within a minute of the request and then waited two to three hours before doing anything with it

Every one of the six failures was a failure of timing: waiting while a clock runs, calling finish six minutes in, before anything had happened, sleeping three hours through an expiry. None was a rule misread, and none an action without consent

Money separates the trials as well. Nine of the ten solved slow-answer trials cost the travellers between 2 and 77 dollars more than the reference run. One cost 8 dollars less: the reference policy is greedy, not optimal

Six new hand-built tasks, family T8, put two or three of the earlier difficulties in one episode and let time run against the agent inside it. No rule of the world was added. Each grows out of an earlier task, and the difference is computed from the two task files

Five of them have a door in the world: cancellations that close two hours after a traveller asks, a replacement flight that leaves within the hour of the airline's notice, a fare that cannot be held while the one who needs it takes 45 minutes to answer, a change offer that lives 20 minutes against an answer that takes 15. Nothing about a door is on the agent's card; it is in the rules the agent can search and on the ticket

The sixth has no door but the end of the episode. It was built on what the retest showed: two steps that each need a slow answer, and a traveller who accepts the new ticket only once the old one is cancelled

The reference policy has an eighth habit, acting when a wish is known. A careless agent with that habit off learns what is wanted, waits, and acts in the last forty minutes. It fails all six tasks and solves earlier tasks, where waiting costs nothing

A first look at the six, 14 trials. The five with a door did not stop the model whose waiting they were built around: where the ticket said the flight left that day, it waited fifty minutes and not three hours. The task with nothing urgent in it stopped that model in one trial of two: it waited three hours, showed quote and new ticket together, and left the traveller with no ticket at all. The lighter model failed one of the five by making proposals and not sending them

items.title: Seven harder tasks, two more habits, and a sheet for every hand-built task
done: Seven more hand-built tasks, 53 development tasks in all. They are built on what the first looks showed: what stopped a model was time, never a rule it did not know. No rule of the world was added and the scripted traveller is unchanged

Two in family T8. One puts both tickets on one booking and leaves a budget with room for exactly one fare on the new day, so that a wrong step costs a quarter of an hour of a slow traveller's time. The other is a twin of an earlier task with the request two hours later: the same steps with 20 idle minutes to spare instead of 140

Three in a new family, T9, with several matters in one watch. Six hours with a delay to leave alone, a ticket that cannot be moved and a cancelled flight. Two matters that overlap on the day of the flights, each with a door of its own. And two travellers who both have to be cancelled and booked again, each step behind an answer of a quarter of an hour, with 105 minutes left

Two in a new family, T10. One traveller cannot pay any fare that suits him, and the other would pay towards his ticket, which she says only when asked. The way through is a proposal with two payers. The scripted traveller and the scoring allowed this from the start; no task had used it

The reference policy has two more habits, ten in all: it lets a traveller who said so pay towards another's ticket, and it keeps watching after the last wish is served. A careless agent lacks each. The one that hands back as soon as nothing is asked of it does what a model did once in the first looks, six minutes into an episode

A first design was dropped. In it a traveller changed his mind twice, and an agent that waited through the first request did one piece of work instead of two and ended 170 dollars better than the reference policy. A task like that rewards the habit the tasks with a clock are there to catch. In the seven that were kept, nothing a later event asks for undoes what an earlier one asked for

Every hand-built task now has a task sheet, a page made to be checked by someone who did not build the task. What can be computed is computed from the task and from scripted play: the hidden facts, the doors, every scripted agent's result, and the reference policy started late every 15 minutes. What is written by hand, the stages, traps and where the agent can read what it needs, is checked against the world wherever it names a minute, a call, an agent, a passage or a sentence of the card
The sheets are shown here with each task

items.title: A review of the harder tasks: a limit for each stage, and checks that a wrong note fails
done: The seven harder tasks and their sheets were reviewed. The review found eight things, each was reproduced with scripted play, and each was true. All seven tasks are kept; five of them were changed in what is said about them, none in its world, its travellers or its events

In the task with two matters and two doors, the sheet had put the purchase of a new ticket under the door of the old one. The old ticket has to be cancelled before cancellations of it close, 150 minutes in. The new ticket is for the next day and can be bought until the watch ends: with the cancellation done in time and the policy kept waiting until minute 155, both travellers are still served. Cancelling and buying are now two stages with a limit each

The checks of a sheet could pass for a note that was wrong. A stage's calls were matched by name and minute, so a refusal of another kind on another order counted. A trap was checked by the name of its careless agent, which could have failed for another reason. Now a stage is bound to its traveller, to the event that sets it off, to a row of the clock, and to calls of the reference run that concern that traveller, end as the note says and carry that traveller's authorization. A door inside the watch is tried: the reference policy is held back until it has closed and has to leave that traveller unserved. A trap is bound to whom the careless agent's run leaves unserved and to something that run shows. A trap that nothing shows is called a design assumption on the page

Tests now turn the checks against wrong notes: a door on the wrong stage, a trap with the wrong traveller or the wrong evidence, a source about somebody else's booking, a source that came after the call that needed it. Each makes exactly the check fail that should. Writing them caught a fault in the first way a door was tried: held in the middle of a step, the policy failed because its offer had run out, not because the door had closed

In the tasks with a shared bill the sheets had written the path of the reference policy as what the task demands. Sharing the fare is needed; the order of the two tickets and the number of proposals are the agent's choice. Her ticket first ends at the same total. Both tickets in one proposal for two seats takes one round of answers fewer and costs 22.57 dollars more, and the agent need not ask whether she would help: a share put in front of her is authorised. The sheets now play these ways

The reference policy let a traveller help with money she then lacked for her own ticket, when the seat sold to the other was the last at its fare. A helper now keeps what her own ticket will cost once that seat is gone, bags counted. The two tasks that use this are solved as before; no earlier task reaches this code

Where a scripted run read what a task needs: an answer of the world now counts only if it was about that traveller's booking and came before the call that needed it, and a value that differs from object to object, such as when a quote runs out, is bound to the object. A passage of the handbook counts only if a search for its heading returns it

Smaller things. Two tickets on one flight, booked apart, each have a door of their own. A page made for a generated task uses the names of its own travellers. The late starts are said to be those of the policy that was played and of the starts that were tried; in one task the worked solution is started late as well and solves it from 45 minutes later than the reference policy does. A change that is tried and refused is no longer listed as a step the tasks need: the order states that its fare cannot be changed

items.title: First trials with a model on the set
done: Condition A on all fifteen tasks with one seat under test, condition C on two tasks, one trial each; every seat played from outside ran and ended without an infrastructure failure

What the trials found, and what was changed: a driver's card did not say that the driver needs a car while theirs is in the shop, so model drivers rented none; the card now says so and the driver is judged on it (cards v3). An insurer that settled the rest of a rental with the other driver on the claim a demand opened was held to have paid what was not owed; an offer the driver accepted now counts as their claim
checked: The set rebuilt on cards v3 and every task admitted again; 722 tests pass, two skipped
